{{short description|None}}

A '''cryptosystem''' is a set of [[cryptography|cryptographic]] [[algorithm]]s that map [[ciphertext]]s and [[plaintext]]s to each other.<ref name="techtarget">{{cite web|url=https://searchsecurity.techtarget.com/definition/cryptosystem|publisher=TechTarget.com|title=cryptosystem|author= Corinne Bernstein|accessdate=Nov 1, 2021}}</ref>

==Private-key cryptosystems==
[[Symmetric-key algorithm|Private-key cryptosystems]] use the same [[key (cryptography)|key]] for [[encryption]] and [[decryption]].

* [[Caesar cipher]]
* [[Substitution cipher]] 
* [[Enigma machine]]
* [[Data Encryption Standard]] 
* [[Twofish]] 
* [[Serpent (cipher)|Serpent]]
* [[Camellia (cipher)|Camellia]]
* [[Salsa20]]
* [[ChaCha20]]
* [[Blowfish (cipher)|Blowfish]]
* [[CAST5]]
* [[Kuznyechik]]
* [[RC4]]
* [[Triple DES|3DES]]
* [[Skipjack (cipher)|Skipjack]]
* [[Secure and Fast Encryption Routine|Safer]]
* [[International Data Encryption Algorithm|IDEA]] 
* [[Advanced Encryption Standard]], also known as AES and Rijndael.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cs.cornell.edu/courses/cs5430/2010sp/TL03.symmetric.html|title=Symmetric-Key Cryptography|last=Roeder|first=Tom|website=www.cs.cornell.edu|language=en|access-date=2017-02-05}}</ref>

==Public-key cryptosystems==
[[Public-key cryptography|Public-key cryptosystems]] use a public key for encryption and a private key for decryption.

* [[Diffie–Hellman key exchange]]
* [[RSA (algorithm)|RSA encryption]]
* [[Rabin cryptosystem]]
* [[Schnorr signature]]
* [[ElGamal encryption]]
* [[Elliptic-curve cryptography]]
* [[Lattice-based cryptography]]
* [[McEliece cryptosystem]]
* [[Multivariate cryptography]]
* [[Isogeny-based cryptography]]
